excerpts:
World of Warcraft Forums

# Anyone know how Saved Variables work?

Community General Discussion

[Thallia-2277436](https://us.forums.blizzard.com/en/wow/u/Thallia-2277436) (Thallia) November 1, 2022, 3:44am 1

Long story short, I changed then deleted a file in a specific character’s Saved Variables. Apparently that broke WoW. I had to uninstall every single version, uninstall Bnet and start over.

So I don’t want to copy over individual character files. Can I just copy over the main Saved Variables from the account folder?

[asil-1629407](https://us.forums.blizzard.com/en/wow/u/asil-1629407) (asil) November 1, 2022, 3:57am 2

The saved variables folder just stores addon configuration information according to the individual addons that create and write the files.

It can’t break the game (generally, I suppose it’s always possible for you to encounter a bug which causes the game to crash as a result of malformed addon data but it shouldn’t be able to). It can only break your interface (via breaking an addon) and even then just disabling all addons should bring you back to the base UI in working condition.

Saved variables are stored in 2 locations. The global location which is under WTF\\Account<youraccountname>\\savedvariables alongside folders named for the servers you have characters on. And the character specific ones in those server folders in subfolders for the individual characters.

The global ones are accessible on all characters, addons can write and share data that can be brought up on any character which is useful for lots of things like sharing unit frame configurations or data on your total gold across characters. It’s also useful for things like being able to copy the addon configuration of one character to another via profiles which is why it’s generally more used. The character specific ones can only be accessed and written while that character is loaded.

So, yes you can copy over just the main, global savedvariables folder and its contents. For the most part it shouldn’t cause issues given the way most addons I’ve seen work.

[Wowpedia](https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/SavedVariables)

### [SavedVariables](https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/SavedVariables)

This is the name given to data which is saved by the user interface and addons between play sessions, storing things such as configurations, collected data, etc. Saved variables are stored in several different files:

note: The addon itself is not stored in saved variables, only data (really settings) for it to use. The addons themselves are stored in the interface folder and if you want to permanently remove one you should delete it from there.

Should you continue to have issues. You can attempt to narrow down the problematic addons by disabling everything and selectively enabling them one by one until the issue occurs to pin-point the problematic addon and reinstall or otherwise fix the issue with that one addon.

results.title: Changing Addon Character Name/Realm - UI and Macro - World of Warcraft Forums

World of Warcraft Forums

# Changing Addon Character Name/Realm

Guides UI and Macro

[Kaldara-2020679](https://us.forums.blizzard.com/en/wow/u/Kaldara-2020679) (Kaldara) June 5, 2021, 4:52pm 1

Over the years I’ve seen a number of posts about how changing a character’s name/realm has caused chaos with regards to some addon settings.

I’ve just completed a name change and found a relatively simple method for making that a smooth transition.

I have not attempted this for Classic or Classic-TBC so while the basic concepts are sound, I can’t vouch for the details. Perhaps someone with characters in those universes could update this with any relevant changes needed for them.

First of all, if you’re using the vanilla UI and no addons you have little or nothing to worry about. Blizzard handles those changes for you relatively smoothly although there can be a short disconnect between your character being ready to play and some of your data catching up with you on realm/faction changes about which you can do little anyway.

You can probably stop reading now.

Also, this will NOT work if your OLD character name is on multiple realms (unless you’re either changing all of them or you don’t mind all of them but the one with the name change getting messed up - like if they’re old toons you keep just for nostalgia).

You’re going to need a tool for making the mass in-file changes. I strongly recommend Notepad++ for this and this guide.

BACK UP YOUR WTF FOLDER FIRST! Both because I might not have caught every possible gotcha here and because you might make an error (either because you didn’t understand or I didn’t make clear some step involved or both).

This first block of instructions assumes you’re only changing (or had forced on you a change in) name.

* Log into the toon under the new name after it’s been changed. You’re not going to play it, you’re just going to force Blizzard and any addons you’re running to create the director(y)(ies) you’ll need.
* Exit the game completely.
* Open File Explorer (assumes Windows here - there’s a Mac equivalent for this but I don’t know what it is - please comment with a note I can include here).
* Locate your …\_retail\_/WTF/Account/<account name>/<realm name> folder.
* Within that folder you’ll see a folder for every toon you’ve ever had on that server (unless you’ve deleted some of the folders previously). Locate the folder for your character’s _previous_ name and open it.
* Select all/copy all the files and folders in there.
* Back out of that folder.
* Locate the folder for your character’s _new_ name and open it.
* Paste everything from the prior folder into this one replacing all files and folders.
* Close File Explorer and open Notepad++.
* From the file menu, choose “Open File As Workspace” and choose the ACCOUNT NAME folder within your …\_retail\_/WTF/Account/<account name>/<realm name> path.
* Right click that folder in the workspace area and select “Find In Files…”.
* When the dialog opens, set the first text box to your character’s OLD name and the second text box to your character’s NEW name. Make sure the “Filters” box reads \*.\*, the “Search Mode” is normal, “Match whole word only”, “Match case”, “Follow current doc.”, and “In hidden folders” are all unchecked, and “In all sub-folders” is checked.
* Click “Replace in Files”.

If you are not changing servers, that’s it.

If you are changing servers, you’ll need to make a few changes to the above:

* You’ll be copying your old character files from the folder under your old realm, not the new one (fairly obvious, but included for completeness).
* You’ll be copying them into the new character under the new realm (again, a Mr. Obvious comment, but not everyone sees the obvious when dealing with technical issues).
* You’ll have to chase down any saved data related to your character that includes the name and server name.

Virtually all of these are kept at the global “Saved Variables” level (it’s something to do with ACE2 and the libraries many addons use for storing data - they don’t exactly follow the design intent that Blizzard laid out with how character-specific data should be stored).

* Expand the ACCOUNT LEVEL folder in the workspace area.
* Right click the “SavedVariables” folder and select “Find in Files…”
* In the first text box, type the OLD Realm Name (as far as I know the default in the ACE2 libraries is the proper name “Earthen Ring” rather than “EarthenRing”). If you find that an addon or two still isn’t behaving, repeat this set of steps with spaces removed from the realm name. If you still have trouble after this repeat this set of steps on the “SavedVariables” files that are under your REALM and CHARACTER folders (note - this deeper editing should not be necessary - I use WeakAuras 2 and ElvUI and both use ACE2 libraries and both worked just fine without it, but . . . just in case).
* DO NOT MAKE A MISTAKE WITH THIS STEP! Click “Find All” (NOT REPLACE ALL).
* In an interactive list at the bottom you’ll see all the “hits” from the search.
* Double-clicking each of the line numbers shown in that list will bring up the file/line in question and if it relates to your character’s NEW name and OLD realm, correct the realm name (perfectly - accuracy counts here).

A search / replace for “ToonName-Realm Name”, “ToonName - Realm Name”, or the “…RealmName” equivalents won’t likely do the job because some addons store the two separately (ElvUI for one). Safest to find every instance of your changed toon’s old realm name and make the changes manually as you go, which will sometimes involve moving things around in tables a bit.

I hope this helps. I know from experience that it can be frustrating when you’ve paid for or had imposed on you a name change and some but not all of your addons stop working correctly. This should help.

# Copying WoW macro and addon settings during a realm transfer

1 Aug, 2012 · Submitted 2012-08-01T07:58:35Z · Read in about 3 min
· (624 Words)  
tags: · [wow](https://chasechristian.com/tags/wow) ·

My guild is transferring from Azgalor-US to Mal’Ganis-US, so I figured this would be a good time to work on a project for copying my macro and addon settings between server profiles. You’ll need to know your new server and character names up front.

Your account information is stored in:

> C:\\Program Files (x86)\\World of Warcraft\\WTF\\Account

Pick the folder for the account that contains the character you’d like to transfer. I have a total of 30 account folders in my current WoW install, which means I’ve logged into 30 accounts from my PC!

## 1 - Make a Backup

First, make a backup of the folder. Make a copy on your desktop or in your My Documents folder to ensure we can revert back if necessary.

## 2 - Prepare the Character Folder

Now, open up your account folder. You should see some server names listed as well as some other things:

[](http://chasechristian.com/wp-content/uploads/2012/07/servers.jpg)

There are a few different sections here. Basically, all of the **files** at this level are safe, as none of them are specific to your server or characters. What we’re concerned with are is the **SavedVariables** and **Realm/Character** **folders** . The files in these specific server folders and the generic SavedVariables folder all contain references to your old character name and your old realm name. We need to go through and re-do all of that in order to have everything carry over smoothly. We’re going to do the character folder first.

Navigate down to the character folder that you’ll be transferring. This puts me in folder:

> C:\\Program Files (x86)\\WoW\\WTF\\Account~~\\Azgalor\\Cure
> 
> 

We’re going to use PowerShell for this next bit, so hopefully you’re using Windows!

Here’s the command:

> gci -recurse | ? {$\_.Attributes -ne “Directory”} | % {(gc $\_.FullName) -replace “ **OLDNAME** ”,” **NEWNAME** ” | sc -path $\_.FullName }
> 
> 

Basically, this command is going to go through and rename every instance of “ **OLDNAME** ” with “ **NEWNAME** ”. We’ll need to run this once or twice. If you have the same toon name on the destination server, then you just need to change your old realm name to your new realm name and everything is peachy. If you are changing your name too, you’ll need to run it again to edit the name. Here’s what I ran exactly:

> C:\\Program Files (x86)\\WoW\\WTF\\Account~~\\Azgalor\\Cure> gci -recurse | ? {$\_.Attributes -ne “Directory”} | % {(gc $\_FullName) -replace “Cure”,“Radsushi” | sc -path $\_.FullName }
> 
> C:\\Program Files (x86)\\WoW\\WTF\\Account~~\\Azgalor\\Cure> gci -recurse | ? {$\_.Attributes -ne “Directory”} | % {(gc $\_.FullName) -replace “Azgalor”,“Mal’Ganis” | sc -path $\_.FullName }
> 
> 

So only two commands here. Each one will take a bit to run, but that’s fine. Once you’re done, we have **PREPARED THE CHARACTER FOLDER** !

## 3 - Prepare the SavedVariables Folder

Navigate to your account’s global SavedVariables folder. This puts me in folder:

> C:\\Program Files (x86)\\WoW\\WTF\\Account\\~~\\SavedVariables\\

Here’s the command:

> gci -recurse | ? {$\_.Attributes -ne “Directory”} | % {(gc $\_.FullName) -replace “ **OLDCHAR - OLDREALM** ”,” **NEWCHAR - NEWREALM** ” | sc -path $\_.FullName }
> 
> 

This time, we’re trying to find something like “Cure - Azgalor” and we want to replace it with “Radsushi - Mal’Ganis”. This won’t fix ALL of your addons, but it should fix most of them. The reason that we don’t run the other commands for this folder is that we don’t want to overwrite the values for your other characters that might be staying behind on the old server.

## 4 - Copy the New Folder

Now we need to copy the character folder to your new realm. If you don’t already have a folder for your new realm, create one. Then, copy your old character folder from your old realm (like \\Azgalor\\Cure) to your new realm (\\Mal’Ganis\\Radsushi):

[](http://chasechristian.com/wp-content/uploads/2012/08/transfer.jpg)

Now you’re done! Kick back and fix the few addons that might’ve screwed up (Postal is one of the few that doesn’t like this process much).

## Navigation

# SavedVariables

[Sign In to Save Save](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fwowwiki-archive.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2FSavedVariables%3Fcollections%3Dsave&uselang=en&metadata=collections-save-button "Sign In to Save") [Edit](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fwowwiki-archive.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2FSavedVariables%3Fveaction%3Dedit&uselang=en&metadata=article-registration-edit-article)

* [History](https://wowwiki-archive.fandom.com/wiki/SavedVariables?action=history)
* [Purge](https://wowwiki-archive.fandom.com/wiki/SavedVariables?action=purge)
* [Talk (0)](https://wowwiki-archive.fandom.com/wiki/Talk:SavedVariables?action=edit&redlink=1)

## What are they? [ ]

This is the name given to data which is saved by the user interface and addons between play sessions, storing things such as configurations, collected data, etc. Saved variables are stored in several different files:

All under _X:/World of Warcraft Install Dir_ /WTF/Account/ _ACCOUNTNAME_ / :

* ./SavedVariables.lua \- only contains settings for Blizzard's own UI
* ./SavedVariables/ _ADDONNAME_ .lua \- global data, per AddOn
* ./ _REALMNAME_ / _CHARNAME_ /SavedVariables/ _ADDONNAME_ .lua \- per-character data, per AddOn

The format of these files is plain LUA script. In theory, you could put actual code in them and have it be loaded, but it would be overwritten the next time variables are saved.

Beware, if you have a copy of the SavedVariables.lua in other locations than the correct one (specifically in your World of Warcraft directory, but possibly not limited to it), then it will be loaded INSTEAD of the one in your account, yet the account one is saved upon logout. This gives the appearance of all addons forgetting their configuration, and can be solved by renaming or deleting the errant copy.

## Resources [ ]

There are numerous resources relating to saved variables:

* Saving variables between game sessions
* The TOC Format \- Description of the .toc file format

The variable doesn't exist until either (a) WoW loads the SavedVariables file at addon-load time, or (b) the addon's own Lua code assigns to it. By default SVs load AFTER the last file in the TOC, but addon code starts running as files load.
